prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You, Mia, have been asked to play a hug role in your best friend Hannah's wedding. You are the maid of honor and you are asked to give a speech at the reception.

User request:
You are Mia and is the maid of honor and the best friend of the bride, Hannah. Hannah is marrying Andrew. Your task is to compose an entertaining and heartfelt maid of honor speech for a wedding. This speech should blend humor, personal anecdotes, and genuine emotion to celebrate the couple's special day.
The audience will be a diverse group of wedding guests, including family members of varying ages, friends, and acquaintances of the bride and groom. They are gathered to celebrate and are looking forward to enjoying the festivities. Your speech should cater to this joyful and celebratory mood, being relatable and engaging to all attendees.
Remember, the goal of your speech is to entertain while sincerely honoring the bride and groom. It's an opportunity to add to the joy and celebration of their special day.
answer:
Good evening, everyone! I’m Mia, Hannah’s best friend and very proud maid of honor. Hannah has trusted me with her secrets, her spare keys, and now a microphone in front of everyone she knows. We’ll find out shortly whether that last one was a good decision.

Being Hannah’s best friend means I’ve had a front-row seat to some wonderful moments—and a few questionable projects.

Once, we decided to bake a birthday cake together. From scratch. With absolutely the confidence you would expect from two people who had never done it before.

By the time we finished, the kitchen looked like a flour bag had exploded, and the cake had developed a noticeable lean. I suggested buying another one. Hannah turned the plate, studied it, and said, “There. That’s the front.”

Then she put candles on it and carried it out like we’d won a baking competition.

That is one of my favorite things about Hannah. She makes things feel worth celebrating. A birthday, a small victory, an ordinary evening that somehow ends with everyone staying for one more cup of tea.

And when things are hard, she shows up just as wholeheartedly. She remembers to ask about the thing you mentioned last week. She lets you tell the same story twice. She knows when you need advice and when you just need someone to sit beside you.

So, naturally, when Andrew came along, I had a few questions. Friendly questions. Asked in a perfectly normal tone, probably.

But what won me over was seeing them together.

Andrew, you listen to Hannah. You make her laugh that completely unfiltered laugh—the one she would definitely have asked me not to demonstrate tonight. And you’re happy to join in when she gets excited about something, even before you’re entirely sure what you’ve agreed to.

Hannah, I’ve loved watching you fall in love with him. I remember wanting every detail after your early dates. Now, seeing you two together, I understand the happiness you were trying to explain.

It means so much to stand beside you today. We’ve shared so many conversations about what the future might look like, and here you are, beginning this part of it with Andrew. I’m incredibly happy for you both.

My wish for your marriage is that you keep enjoying each other’s company through all of it: the big adventures, the quiet evenings, and the important negotiations about what to have for dinner.

And if something turns out a little crooked, I hope you’ll turn the plate together and find the front.

Everyone, please raise a glass.

To Hannah and Andrew: a lifetime of laughter, kindness, and plenty of reasons to celebrate. Cheers!
